chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from 'Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from 'Abdullah ibn Muskan, from Dawud ibn Farqad, from Abu Sa'id al-Zuhri, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Pausing at the doubtful matter is better than storming into destruction; and your refraining from narrating a hadith you have not fully verified is better than your narrating a hadith you have not mastered.

key_terms.الشُّبْهَة: Doubt, ambiguity, or unclear matter — a technical term in Islamic ethics and jurisprudence for situations where the lawful and unlawful are indistinguishable
key_terms.الِاقْتِحَام: Storming into, plunging recklessly — connotes impetuous action without adequate forethought
key_terms.الْهَلَكَة: Destruction, perdition, ruin — spiritual or physical catastrophe resulting from rash action
key_terms.تُحْصِهِ: To count, comprehend, master completely — implies full command of the material being transmitted

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Baqir say about caution in doubtful matters and hadith narration?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) offers two parallel maxims urging extreme caution in religious matters. The first warns against recklessly proceeding when faced with ambiguity or uncertainty, likening it to rushing into ruin. The second specifically addresses hadith transmission, directing that one should remain silent rather than transmit a tradition one does not fully grasp — a significant principle in the early Shia scholarly community that was wrestling with the proliferation of traditions and their careful verification.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ali Bin Al Nu’man, from Abdullah Bin Muskan, from Dawood Bin Farqad, from Abu Saeed Al Zuhry, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘
The pausing at the doubtful (vagueness) is better than storming into the destruction; and refraining from reporting a Hadeeth which you have not verified, is better than your reporting a Hadeeth’.
en.sarwar: 9. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Ali ibn an-Ni‘man from ‘Abdallah ibn Muskan from Daiwud ibn Farqad from abu Sa‘id al-Zuhri from abu Ja’far (a.s.) who has said the following.

“Holding back in an uncertain conditions is better than indulging in a destructive case. Your ignoring a Hadith that you do not narrate is better than your narrating a Hadith that you have not verified.”
